categories.name: What you'll lose
categories.question: Does it tell people what they will have to do without: their job, their RAM, their privacy, their say?

levels.0: Nobody is asked to give anything up.
levels.1: A small or far-off loss, or one he says won't happen.
levels.3: A real loss to many: a craft, a feed, a share of the web's traffic.
levels.5: Taken outright, at scale: thousands of jobs, a whole trade, everything on your screen.

award.name: The Brioche Prize
award.for: for telling the public what it will have to do without

categories.name: Condescension
categories.question: Does it talk down to the people it is about?

levels.0: Speaks to them as equals, or with some humility.
levels.1: A hint of looking down, in otherwise plain words.
levels.3: Their worries are brushed aside, or they are told what is good for them.
levels.5: Tells them their work, their view or they themselves don't count.

award.name: The Powdered Wig
award.for: for looking down on the public from the greatest height

categories.name: Tone-deafness
categories.question: Does it miss how it sounds to someone without a billion dollars?

levels.0: Reads the room: nobody without a billion dollars would wince.
levels.1: One line that grates, in an otherwise reasonable moment.
levels.3: Said to the people it costs, in the wrong room or at the wrong moment, as if it were good news.
levels.5: Hardship sold as an opportunity, at the worst possible moment, by the man who can afford it.

award.name: The Hall of Mirrors
award.for: for seeing nothing but his own reflection

categories.name: Doom
categories.question: Does it predict catastrophe, often while selling the cause of it?

levels.0: No catastrophe forecast; optimism, however grand, scores nothing here.
levels.1: A mild or narrow worry, hedged or in passing.
levels.3: Upheaval for society at large, forecast as coming.
levels.5: The end of humanity, or of work as we know it, said out loud.

award.name: Après Moi, le Déluge
award.for: for forecasting the flood and selling tickets to it

categories.name: Hypocrisy
categories.question: Does it contradict what the speaker or his company says or does elsewhere?

levels.0: No contradiction on record; selling the thing he talks about is not one.
levels.1: A small or arguable clash with something on record, named in the reason.
levels.3: Clearly at odds with something he or his company said or did, named in the reason.
levels.5: The opposite of what he said, or the very thing he ruled out.

award.name: The Petit Hameau
award.for: named after the toy village where Marie Antoinette played at peasant life

topStatement.name: The Cake
topStatement.for: for the single statement that raised the most pitchforks
